set.body:
`.compute_statistical_volumes()` (R/bids_export.R:1789-1806) builds its output
with `stat_matrices[[i]] <- stat_value`. When `stat_value` is NULL that
assignment *deletes* the slot rather than storing it, so the list stays short.
If every contrast resolves to NULL the list is empty, the function returns NULL
at :1806, and `.save_contrasts_by_stat()` (:741) / `.save_contrasts_by_stat_nifti()`
(:786) skip the write with no error, no warning, and exit 0.

Meanwhile `.predict_output_files()` (:208-233) has already claimed those
filenames for the overwrite pre-check, so predict and write disagree about what
the run produces.

This is the #213 failure mode -- contrasts vanish silently -- in the DEFAULT
strategy (`by_stat`). The `by_contrast` path hard-errors on the same input
(:858-864, :937-943), so one malformed contrast produces two different outcomes
depending on `strategy`.

The #220 sentinel used to reach this path; after the fix on
`fix/220-empty-contrast-table` it no longer does, but a genuinely malformed
contrast row still would.

Latent index hazard in the same block: `contrast_names[i] <- contrast_data$name[i]`
is written at position `i` while `stat_matrices` may have been shortened by the
NULL deletion, and `valid_indices` is computed only from `stat_matrices`. The two
vectors are maintained by different mechanisms.

Fix direction: store NULLs explicitly (e.g. `stat_matrices[i] <- list(stat_value)`),
keep names and matrices in one structure, and make a contrast that cannot be
written a diagnostic rather than a silent skip.
set.title: write_results by_stat silently drops contrasts that resolve to NULL
